items.title: The declared driven model: prescribed time-dependent energy families, propagator evolution and the two-level drive models
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, in the state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The readings below are the reading of clause (iv) of P4 for the page's models; clause (iv) records that a prescribed time-dependent family is **a different model assumption** from the autonomous one, and clause (b) below adopts it.

**(b) Prescribed energy family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair, fix a nonempty compact interval $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ of physical times (seconds), the declared state space $\mathfrak H$ of the system, a value $\hbar>0$ of the reduced Planck constant as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and a **prescribed family** $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators on $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) in one of the following three **regularity classes**, whose hypotheses are part of the model declaration:

- **(i) Bounded norm-continuous class.** $D(H(t))=\mathfrak H$ for every $t$; each $H(t)\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is self-adjoint ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); $t\mapsto H(t)$ is norm-continuous on $I$ ([[def-operator-norm]]); and $K:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H(t)\|/\hbar<\infty$.
- **(ii) Bounded-control class.** $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$, where $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H$ and $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V(t)\|=v(t)$, $v:=\sup_{t\in I}v(t)<\infty$.
- **(iii) Common-domain class.** There is a dense linear subspace $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]], for instance $Y=D(H_{0})$ with the graph norm of a self-adjoint $H_{0}$), with $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t$, each $H(t)$ self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$, and $t\mapsto H(t)$ of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$.

The family, its class and its data are **prescribed**: no field equation, source model, back-reaction or feedback of the system on the source is assumed, and no claim is made that any laboratory arrangement realizes the family. The family is coupled to the system through the material hypotheses of the page or of the item that declares a specific model (for instance a magnetic-moment or electric-dipole coupling, or the external-source Coulomb family of the page's adiabatic models); the reading of $H(t)$ as the energy of the declared system is a model assumption.

**(c) The model's evolution.** The **driven model** declares that the time evolution of the system between times $s,t\in I$ is carried by a family $U(t,s)$ of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$ with
$$U(s,s)=I,\qquad U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)\quad(r,s,t\in I),\qquad U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t),$$
jointly strongly continuous in $(t,s)$, solving the time-dependent Schroedinger equation on $I$ in the sense of the class:
in class (i) $U$ is the unique norm-continuous solution of $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ with $U(s,s)=I$ constructed by the Dyson series of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] (whose hypothesis is exactly the norm-continuity of the bounded self-adjoint family);
in class (ii) $U$ is the mild propagator constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]], satisfying $U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^tE(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr$ for every $\psi\in\mathfrak H$, with $E(u)=e^{-iuH_{0}/\hbar}$ the autonomous flow of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]];
in class (iii) $U$ is the strong propagator of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]] with physical generator $A=H/\hbar$, preserving $Y$, for which $t\mapsto U(t,s)y$ is $C^1$ in $\mathfrak H$ with $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y$ for every $y\in Y$.
In each class the cited item is what makes the declaration well posed: it constructs the family and proves uniqueness under the class hypotheses. The model asserts nothing beyond those hypotheses; in particular it asserts no invariant domain and no strong equation for $H_{0}$-domain vectors in class (ii), and no common domain in classes (i) and (ii).

On a singleton interval $I=\{a\}$, the evolution declaration consists only of $U(a,a)=I$; all differential assertions in these class readings apply only when $a<b$, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints.

**(d) State and outcome readings.** The **evolved preparation** at time $t$ of a preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ is $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$; it is a preparation of the model in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] for every $t$, by unitarity of $U(t,s)$ and [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]. A pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$ evolves to the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ with $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)\ne0$. The **outcome law at time $t$** of an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) in that preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}$, the reading of P2; the definition records the timing convention once and asserts nothing about how or when a record is produced.

**(e) Energy-basis amplitudes and level populations.** In class (ii), let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ and $E_{j}\in\mathbb R$ (a complete orthonormal family of eigenvectors is not assumed here). For $s\le t$ and labels $i,j$ the **transition amplitude from $i$ at time $s$ to $j$ at time $t$** is the scalar
$$A_{ji}(t,s):=e^{iE_{j}(t-s)/\hbar}\,\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle ,$$
and the **transition probability** is $p_{ji}(t,s):=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$. If additionally $E_{j}$ is a simple eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ with spectral projection $P_{j}=E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})$ onto $\mathbb C\varphi_{j}$, then the definition *states*, as the reading of P2, the identity
$$p_{ji}(t,s)=\mu^{H_{0}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{j}\})=\|E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})\psi(t)\|^{2},\qquad \psi(t)=U(t,s)\varphi_{i},$$
which follows from the rank-one form of $P_{j}$ and the normalization $\|\varphi_{j}\|=1$; $p_{ji}$ is the reading of the outcome probability of the value $E_{j}$ of the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ in the evolved preparation, and it is a property of the declared model, not a measured frequency.

**(f) Declared two-level drive models.** Let $(\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z})$ be the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) acting on $\mathbb C^{2}$ in the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]), let $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega\in\mathbb R$, and put $H_{0}:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}$ (class (i) with $I$ any compact interval). The **circular two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),$$
and the **linear two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}\bigr).$$
The real parameters $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ represent angular frequencies of dimension duration$^{-1}$, read in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; their numerical values are expressed in that unit, so $\omega t$ is dimensionless and $\hbar\omega_{0}$ and $\hbar\Omega_{1}$ have energy units; $\omega_{0}$ is the **splitting frequency** of the model (the level gap is $\hbar|\omega_{0}|$), $\omega$ the **drive frequency**, $\Omega_{1}$ the **transverse coupling**, and $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$ the **detuning**. Populations of the level pair are the diagonal entries $\langle P_{\bullet}\psi,\psi\rangle$ of the orthogonal projections $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$ in the evolved vector $\psi(t)$. The two families are model data: no identification with a laboratory spin, molecule or field, and no relation of $\Omega_{1}$ to a field amplitude, is asserted; such an identification is a tested identification in the sense of P7.

**(g) Status and scope.** Clauses (b), (c), (f) are adopted model assumptions and readings; the existence and uniqueness of the propagator in each class is cited mathematics, not a consequence of P1, P2 or P4. The model asserts no open-system or environment coupling, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no thermalization or equilibration, no long-time limit and no empirical record; the identification of the family's parameters with laboratory fields and of the system with a laboratory sample is made, if at all, only in separately declared models with their own uncertainty.

items.physical_scope: The driven-dynamics model of a declared system of the framework: a prescribed time-dependent family of self-adjoint energy operators in one of three declared regularity classes (bounded norm-continuous on a compact interval; a fixed self-adjoint part plus a strongly continuous bounded self-adjoint control; a common-domain C^1 family), the unitary two-time propagator declared to carry the state evolution, the reading of preparations and outcome laws at the running time, the energy-basis transition amplitudes and level populations, and the two declared two-level drive models (circular and linear polarization). The definition fixes terminology and readings only: it adopts the driven-evolution assumption as an additional model assumption beyond P4, and asserts no existence theorem (supplied by the cited mathematics in each class), no laboratory realization, no measurement, no open system, no equilibration and no empirical result.

items.title: The interaction picture of the declared driven model: readings, the interaction propagator and picture equivalence of outcome laws
items.statement:
**(a) Setting.** Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of its clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on its exact dense domain $D(H_{0})$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $v=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$ on $D(H_{0})$, and $U(t,s)$ is the mild propagator of clause (c)(ii) constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]. The readings of P1 and P2 are those of [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; all times lie in $I$ and are read in seconds as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The free-flow factor.** The **free-flow factor** of the model is the autonomous flow of the unperturbed part,
$$E(t):=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] applied to the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$; it is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on all real arguments. This auxiliary group supplies $E(-t)$ and $E(t-s)$ even when those arguments lie outside $I$; the physical driven evaluation times $s,t$ remain in $I$. The **interaction-picture control** is the family $V_{I}:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$,
$$V_{I}(t):=E(-t)V(t)E(t),$$
which is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V_{I}(t)\|=\|V(t)\|\le v$. The **interaction propagator** is
$$U_{I}(t,s):=E(-t)U(t,s)E(s)\qquad(s,t\in I),$$
and the model's clause (c)(ii) supplies, as the cited theorem proves, the decomposition
$$U(t,s)=E(t)U_{I}(t,s)E(-s).$$
The interaction propagator is unitary, jointly strongly continuous, satisfies $U_{I}(s,s)=I$ and the cocycle $U_{I}(t,r)=U_{I}(t,s)U_{I}(s,r)$, and its first-endpoint map is strongly differentiable with
$$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}U_{I}(t,s)\psi=V_{I}(t)U_{I}(t,s)\psi\qquad(\psi\in\mathfrak H),$$
all as supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]; these are readings of that theorem in the model's vocabulary, not new assumptions.

**(c) Interaction states and preparations.** For a Schroedinger-picture state vector $\psi(t)=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ the **interaction-picture state** is
$$\psi_{I}(t):=E(-t)\psi(t),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad\psi_{I}(t)=U_{I}(t,s)\psi_{I}(s),$$
and for a preparation $\rho$ with $\rho(t)=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ the **interaction-picture preparation** is
$$\rho_{I}(t):=E(-t)\rho(t)E(t),$$
which is again a preparation of the model by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]; for a pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$, $[\psi_{I}(t)]$ is pure. The map $\psi(t)\mapsto\psi_{I}(t)$ is unitary at every $t$, so $\|\psi_{I}(t)\|=\|\psi(t)\|$.

**(d) The two pictures assign the same outcome laws.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ bounded and let $A_{I}(t):=E(-t)AE(t)$ be its interaction-picture representative, which is again a bounded self-adjoint observable with $E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)=E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)$ for every Borel set $B$ by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] applied to the flow $E$ of the self-adjoint $T=-H_{0}/\hbar$. Then for every preparation $\rho$ specified at $s$ and every $t\in I$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_{I}(t)}_{\rho_{I}(t)}(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
because $\rho(t)=E(t)\rho_{I}(t)E(-t)$ and $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(E(t)\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)\bigr)$ by cyclicity of the trace; equivalently, for a pure preparation, $\|E_{A}(B)\psi(t)\|=\|E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)\psi_{I}(t)\|$. This identity is the precise sense in which the two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; it is a reading of P2 together with the cited mathematics, not a claim about apparatuses.

**(e) Energy-basis transition amplitudes.** Let $\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\in D(H_{0})$ be unit eigenvectors, $H_{0}\varphi_{a}=E_{a}\varphi_{a}$, $H_{0}\varphi_{b}=E_{b}\varphi_{b}$, and let $A_{ba}(t,s)$ and $p_{ba}(t,s)$ be the transition amplitude and probability of clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]. Then
$$A_{ba}(t,s)=e^{is(E_{a}-E_{b})/\hbar}\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle ,\qquad\text{hence}\qquad p_{ba}(t,s)=\bigl|\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2},$$
by the decomposition of clause (b) and $E(-s)\varphi_{a}=e^{isE_{a}/\hbar}\varphi_{a}$, $\langle E(t)\chi,\varphi_{b}\rangle=e^{-itE_{b}/\hbar}\langle\chi,\varphi_{b}\rangle$; the phases are of modulus one ([[def-inner-product-space]]). The transition probability is therefore computable in either picture, and the definition records this as the reading used by the page's amplitude theorem; no measurement frequency or rate is defined.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) are readings of the declared driven model, of clauses (b)-(e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]], and of P1 and P2, in the vocabulary of the cited mathematics. The interaction picture is a change of description of the same model: it adds no assumption, no physical process, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it asserts nothing about detectors, records or the laboratory realization of the model.

items.title: The two-level rotating frame: conjugation identities, the transformed families and invariance of the level populations
items.statement:
Let $(\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z)$ be the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), acting on $\mathbb C^2$ in the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ of that clause, so that $\sigma_z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, $\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$ and $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$; write $I$ for the identity and let $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ be the orthogonal projections onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow}$ and $\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$. Let $\hbar>0$, $\omega,\omega_0,\Omega_1\in\mathbb R$, put $\Delta:=\omega_0-\omega$ and, for $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$R(t):=\cos\!\Bigl(\frac{\omega t}{2}\Bigr)I+i\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{\omega t}{2}\Bigr)\sigma_z .$$
Then:

(a) *Frame.* For every $t$ the matrix $R(t)$ is unitary with $R(0)=I$, the map $R$ is of class $C^{\infty}$ with
$$R'(t)=\frac{i\omega}{2}\,\sigma_zR(t),$$
and $R(t)P_{\uparrow}R(t)^{*}=P_{\uparrow}$, $R(t)P_{\downarrow}R(t)^{*}=P_{\downarrow}$.

(b) *Conjugation.* For every $t$,
$$R(t)\sigma_xR(t)^{*}=\cos(\omega t)\,\sigma_x-\sin(\omega t)\,\sigma_y,\qquad R(t)\sigma_yR(t)^{*}=\sin(\omega t)\,\sigma_x+\cos(\omega t)\,\sigma_y,\qquad R(t)\sigma_zR(t)^{*}=\sigma_z .$$

(c) *Circular drive.* For the family $H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_x+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_y)\bigr)$ one has, for every $t$,
$$R(t)H_{\mathrm c}(t)R(t)^{*}+i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\Delta\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x\bigr),$$
which is a constant Hermitian matrix independent of $t$.

(d) *Linear drive.* For the family $H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1\cos(\omega t)\sigma_x\bigr)$ put
$$A:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\Delta\sigma_z+\frac{\Omega_1}{2}\sigma_x\Bigr),\qquad B:=\frac{\hbar\Omega_1}{8}\bigl(\sigma_x+i\sigma_y\bigr).$$
Then for every $t$
$$R(t)H_{\mathrm l}(t)R(t)^{*}+i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}=A+e^{2i\omega t}B+e^{-2i\omega t}B^{*},$$
and $\|A\|\le\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(|\Delta|+\frac{|\Omega_1|}{2}\bigr)$, $\|B\|=\frac{\hbar|\Omega_1|}{4}$.

(e) *Transformation of the dynamics.* Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H:\mathbb R\to\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^2)$ be continuous with Hermitian values, let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C^2$ be of class $C^1$ with
$$i\hbar\psi'(t)=H(t)\psi(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
and put $\psi_R:=R\psi$ and $H^{R}(t):=R(t)H(t)R(t)^{*}+i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}$. Then $\psi_R$ is of class $C^1$ and satisfies $i\hbar\psi_R'(t)=H^{R}(t)\psi_R(t)$ for every $t$; the family $H^{R}$ is continuous with Hermitian values. Consequently, if $U$ is the unitary propagator of the norm-continuous family $H$ supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]], then
$$U^{R}(t,s):=R(t)U(t,s)R(s)^{*}\qquad(s,t\in\mathbb R)$$
is the unitary propagator of $H^{R}$: it satisfies $i\hbar\partial_tU^{R}(t,s)=H^{R}(t)U^{R}(t,s)$, $U^{R}(s,s)=I$, the cocycle, and $U^{R}(t,s)^{*}=U^{R}(s,t)$. Moreover for every solution $\psi$ of the $H$-equation, every $t\in\mathbb R$ and both signs $\bullet\in\{\uparrow,\downarrow\}$,
$$\bigl\langle P_{\bullet}\psi(t),\psi(t)\bigr\rangle=\bigl\langle P_{\bullet}\psi_R(t),\psi_R(t)\bigr\rangle .$$

The lemma is a statement of finite-dimensional linear algebra and calculus for the displayed matrices; no physical identification, no measurement and no asymptotic claim is made.

items.title: The bounded norm-continuous driven model: unique unitary propagator, Dyson truncation budget and outcome-law error
items.statement:
Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded norm-continuous class** of clause (b)(i): $I=[a,b]$ is the declared compact time interval, $\mathfrak H$ the state space of the declared system, $\hbar>0$, and $H:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is norm-continuous with self-adjoint values, $K:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H(t)\|/\hbar<\infty$. Let $U_{0}(t,s)=I$ and $U_{n+1}(t,s)=\int_{s}^{t}A(r)U_{n}(r,s)\,dr$ with $A(r)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H(r)$ be the oriented Dyson iterates of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]], and let $U(t,s)=\sum_{n\ge0}U_{n}(t,s)$ be its norm-convergent propagator; for $N\in\mathbb N_{0}$ put $R_{N}(t,s):=U(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^{N}U_{n}(t,s)$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the latter for the outcome-law reading of P2. Then:

(a) *Well-posedness of the declared model.* The family $U$ is the unique family of bounded operators on $\mathfrak H$ that is jointly norm-continuous on $I\times I$, unitary-valued, satisfies $U(s,s)=I$ and the cocycle $U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)$, and solves $i\hbar\partial_{t}U(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ together with its second-endpoint equation $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(t,s)=-U(t,s)H(s)$ in operator norm. In particular the model's clause (c)(i) declaration has exactly one solution: the driven model in the bounded norm-continuous class is well posed.

(b) *Truncation budget.* For all $s,t\in I$ and all $N\in\mathbb N_{0}$, with $\tau:=|t-s|$,
$$\bigl\|R_{N}(t,s)\bigr\|\le e^{K\tau}\,\frac{(K\tau)^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \|U(t,s)-I\|\le e^{K\tau}-1 .$$
In particular $\|R_{1}(t,s)\|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$ and $\|R_{2}(t,s)\|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{3}/6$.

(c) *Evolved states and outcome laws.* For every preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ the operator $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ is a preparation of the model with $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ for every $t\in I$, and the specification is consistent with the cocycle: evolving first from $s$ to $r$ and then from $r$ to $t$ gives the same preparation. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi(s)$ the vector $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ is unit and spans a pure preparation for every $t$. For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, the number $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)$ is the model's outcome probability at time $t$.

(d) *Error of the unnormalized truncated quadratic estimate.* Let $\psi(s)$ be a unit vector, put $\psi^{N}(t):=\sum_{n=0}^{N}U_{n}(t,s)\psi(s)$ and let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ bounded. Then for every $t\in I$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\bigl|\mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)-\mu^{A}_{\psi^{N}(t)}(B)\bigr|\le (1+\|\sum_{n=0}^NU_n(t,s)\|)\,\|R_N(t,s)\|\le 2\,e^{K\tau}\frac{(K\tau)^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},$$
where the truncated quantity is the unnormalized quadratic form $\mu^{A}_{\psi^{N}(t)}(B):=\|E_{A}(B)\psi^{N}(t)\|^{2}$ of the truncated vector, whose norm is at most $e^{K\tau}$. It is an approximation to the normalized exact Born law and need not itself be a probability law; for $N=1$ the bound also implies the looser estimate $2e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}$.

(e) *Scope.* The theorem is conditional on the bounded norm-continuous class, on the compactness of $I$ and on $K<\infty$. It asserts no existence or uniqueness statement for unbounded families (which are treated in their own classes), no uniform-in-time approximation, no rate or decay, no measurement or apparatus model, and no comparison with any recorded data.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 2.3 printed pages 15-17 (PDF pages 15-17): the time-ordered exponential series of a time-dependent Hamiltonian and its truncation

items.title: The bounded-control driven model: mild propagator, interaction-picture evolution and equivalence of the two readings
items.statement:
Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space, $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $v:=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$ on $D(H_{0})$, and adopt the interaction-picture readings of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-interaction-picture]]: $E(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$, $V_{I}(t)=E(-t)V(t)E(t)$, $U_{I}(t,s)=E(-t)U(t,s)E(s)$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the latter for the outcome-law reading of P2. Let $U(t,s)$ be the mild propagator constructed by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]. Then:

(a) *Well-posedness of the declared model.* $U$ is the unique family of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$, jointly strongly continuous on $I\times I$, with $U(s,s)=I$, $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$ and the cocycle $U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)$, satisfying the vectorwise mild Schroedinger identity
$$U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}E(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr\qquad(\psi\in\mathfrak H,\ s,t\in I);$$
so the model's clause (c)(ii) declaration has exactly one solution. For $\psi,\varphi\in D(H_{0})$ the scalar curve $t\mapsto\langle U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\rangle$ is continuously differentiable on $I$ with
$$\frac{d}{dt}\bigl\langle U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\bigr\rangle=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\Bigl[\bigl\langle U(t,s)\psi,H_{0}\varphi\bigr\rangle+\bigl\langle V(t)U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\bigr\rangle\Bigr].$$
No invariance of $D(H_{0})$ under $U$, no strong full Schroedinger equation for its domain vectors, and no operator-norm differentiability of $U$ with respect to the unbounded generator are asserted.

(b) *Interaction picture.* For every $s,t\in I$ and every $\psi\in\mathfrak H$ the interaction state $\psi_{I}(t):=E(-t)U(t,s)\psi(s)$ satisfies $\psi_{I}(t)=U_{I}(t,s)\psi_{I}(s)$, and its first-endpoint map is strongly differentiable with $i\hbar\partial_{t}\psi_{I}(t)=V_{I}(t)\psi_{I}(t)$; the interaction propagator is unitary with the cocycle and $U_{I}(t,s)^{*}=U_{I}(s,t)$, and its strong truncation bound is $\|U_{I}(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^{N}D_{n}(t,s)\|\le e^{K(t-s)}(K(t-s))^{N+1}/(N+1)!$ for $s\le t$ with $K=v/\hbar$.

(c) *Equivalence of the two readings.* For every preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$, every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ with $A$ bounded, every $t\in I$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, the Schroedinger reading and the interaction reading give the same outcome probability:
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_{I}(t)}_{\rho_{I}(t)}(B),\qquad A_{I}(t)=E(-t)AE(t),\quad \rho_{I}(t)=E(-t)\rho(t)E(t),$$
and for pure preparations $\|\psi_{I}(t)\|=\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(s)\|$. For eigenvectors $\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}$ of $H_{0}$ as in clause (e) of the model, the transition probabilities of the two pictures agree,
$$p_{ba}(t,s)=\bigl|\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2}=\bigl|\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2}.$$

(d) *Scope.* The theorem is conditional on the bounded-control class; the mild identity, not a strong equation on $D(H_{0})$, is the evolution equation it establishes, and it asserts nothing about unbounded controls, invariant domains, measurement records, detectors, rates or empirical data.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Chapter 5 printed pages 123-131 (PDF pages 135-143): mild evolution equations and the interaction picture for a bounded time-dependent perturbation of a self-adjoint operator

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 2.3 printed pages 15-17 (PDF pages 15-17): Dyson's formula for a time-dependent Hamiltonian with a time-independent part

items.physical_scope: The bounded-control driven model of the declared system: existence, uniqueness and unitary character of the mild two-time propagator of H(t) = H0 + V(t), the vectorwise mild Schroedinger identity, the weak Schroedinger identity on the domain of H0, the interaction-picture state evolution and control, and the equivalence of the Schroedinger and interaction readings of the outcome laws. The theorem is conditional on a self-adjoint H0 and a strongly continuous bounded self-adjoint control and asserts no invariant domain, no strong full Schroedinger equation for domain vectors, no measurement and no empirical result.

items.title: First-order transition amplitudes for a bounded control: Dyson remainder, the sinusoidal drive with its co- and counter-rotating parts, and the outcome-probability error
items.statement:
Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space, $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$, $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values, $v=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ and $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$; let $U(t,s)$ be the mild propagator and put $K:=v/\hbar$. Let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]) — a complete family is not required — and fix labels $i,j\in J$ and $s\le t$ in $I$, with $\tau:=t-s$ and $\Delta:=E_{j}-E_{i}$. Let $A_{ji}(t,s)=e^{iE_j\tau/\hbar}\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle$ be the transition amplitude of clause (e) of the model and define its first-order term
$$A^{(1)}_{ji}(t,s):=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}e^{i\Delta(r-s)/\hbar}\bigl\langle V(r)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\,dr .$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Exact amplitude with Dyson remainder.* There is a remainder $R_{ji}(t,s)$ with
$$A_{ji}(t,s)=\delta_{ij}+A^{(1)}_{ji}(t,s)+R_{ji}(t,s),\qquad |R_{ji}(t,s)|\le e^{K\tau}\frac{(K\tau)^{2}}{2},$$
and if $\eta:I\to[0,\infty)$ is measurable and integrable, $\|V(r)-V_{0}(r)\|\le\eta(r)$ for $r\in I$, and $V_{0}:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ has self-adjoint values with integrable scalar coefficient $r\mapsto\langle V_{0}(r)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle$, then the corresponding first-order amplitude differs from $A^{(1)}_{ji}$ by at most $\frac{1}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}\eta(r)\,dr$.

(b) *Sinusoidal control.* Let $W\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ be self-adjoint, $\omega,\vartheta\in\mathbb R$, and suppose $V(r)=W\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ for $r\in I$. Put $\vartheta_{0}:=\omega s+\vartheta$ and decompose
$$A^{(1)}_{ji}=a_{+}+a_{-},\qquad a_{\pm}:=-\frac{i}{2\hbar}\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle e^{\mp i\vartheta_{0}}\,\frac{e^{i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)\tau/\hbar}-1}{i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)/\hbar},$$
with the convention that the quotient is the limit $\tau$ when $\Delta\mp\hbar\omega=0$. Then the *co-rotating* term $a_{+}$ (the one whose denominator vanishes at $\Delta=\hbar\omega$) satisfies
$$|a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\,\frac{\bigl|\sin\bigl((\Delta-\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar)\bigr)\bigr|}{|\Delta-\hbar\omega|},\qquad\text{and at }\Delta=\hbar\omega:\quad |a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\frac{\tau}{2\hbar},$$
and the *counter-rotating* term satisfies $|a_{-}|\le|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|$ whenever $\Delta+\hbar\omega\ne0$.

(c) *Outcome probability.* The model's transition probability is $p_{ji}(t,s)=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$; with $\varepsilon:=e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$ and $A^{(1)}:=A^{(1)}_{ji}$, for distinct labels $i\ne j$
$$\bigl|p_{ji}(t,s)-|A^{(1)}|^{2}\bigr|\le 2|A^{(1)}|\,\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2},$$
and for $i=j$ the survival probability obeys the analogous bound $\bigl|p_{ii}(t,s)-|1+A^{(1)}|^{2}\bigr|\le(2+2|A^{(1)}|)\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2}$; in both cases the exact outcome probability is controlled by the first-order term and the explicit Dyson error of clause (a).

(d) *Scope.* The statements are finite-time and conditional on the bounded control and on the orthonormal eigenfamily; the remainder bound grows like $\tau^{2}e^{K\tau}$ and no long-time limit, transition rate, exponential decay, continuum density of states or Fermi golden rule is asserted, and no measured frequency, count or rate is claimed.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.3 printed pages 213-214 (PDF pages 221-222): the first-order amplitude a_k(t) (9.47) and the transition probability of equation (9.48) for a harmonic perturbation V(t) = V0 exp(i omega t), with the resonant sin^2 growth

items.physical_scope: First-order transition amplitudes and their error in the bounded-control driven model: the exact amplitude in an orthonormal family of H0 eigenvectors, its first-order term with the explicit Dyson remainder bound, the closed evaluation for a sinusoidal control split into co-rotating and counter-rotating parts with their bounds, the linear growth at resonance, and the resulting bound on the outcome probability. The theorem is conditional on a bounded self-adjoint control and an orthonormal eigenfamily of H0; it asserts no long-time limit, no Fermi golden rule, no continuum density of states, no transition rate, no decay and no empirical result.

items.title: The common-domain driven model: strong propagator with domain invariance, and the driven oscillator as its declared instance
items.statement:
Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **common-domain class** of clause (b)(iii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ is a dense linear subspace that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$, $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t\in I=[a,b]$, every $H(t)$ is self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and $t\mapsto H(t)$ is of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]); put $L:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H'(t)\|_{\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H)}<\infty$ and $A(t):=H(t)/\hbar$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Well-posedness of the declared model.* There is a family $U(t,s)$, $a\le s\le t\le b$ on $I$, of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$ with $U(s,s)=I$, the cocycle $U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)$, joint strong continuity in $(t,s)$, and:
$$U(t,s)Y=Y,\qquad \|U(t,s)y\|_Y\le C_{I}\|y\|_Y\quad(y\in Y), \qquad i\hbar\,\partial_{t}U(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y\quad(y\in Y),$$
where the derivative is in $\mathfrak H$ and $C_{I}<\infty$ is independent of the endpoints and depends on the actual graph equivalence of $Y$ with $D(H(t)/\hbar)$ as well as $I$ and $L/\hbar$; this family is unique among bounded families with the same strong equation on $Y$, $U(s,s)=I$ and locally bounded strong orbits. The model's clause (c)(iii) declaration therefore has exactly one solution.

(b) *Reverse and adjoint equations.* With $U(s,t):=U(t,s)^{-1}$ one has $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$ and $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(t,s)y=-U(t,s)H(s)y$ for $y\in Y$; equivalently $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(s,t)y=H(s)U(s,t)y$. The domain maps $(t,s)\mapsto U(t,s)|_{Y}$ are jointly strongly continuous in $\mathcal B(Y)$.

(c) *Declared instance: the driven oscillator.* Let $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and let $(H_{\mathrm{osc}},Q)$ be the energy and position observables of the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (b), (c) on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$, with $Y=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ carrying the graph norm, and let $f\in C^{1}(I;\mathbb R)$. Declare, as a further model assumption of the pair, the **driven oscillator family**
$$H(t):=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q\qquad(t\in I),$$
read as the system's energy at time $t$, with $f(t)Q$ in joules for $f(t)$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$. Then for every $t$ the operator $H(t)$ is self-adjoint on the single domain $Y$, the family belongs to $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,L^{2}))$ with derivative $-f'(t)Q$, and the hypotheses of clause (a) are satisfied with $\mathfrak H=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$; consequently the driven oscillator has a unique strong propagator preserving $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and satisfying $i\hbar\partial_{t}U(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y$ for $y\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$.

(d) *Scope.* The theorem is conditional on the common-domain regularity class and on the cited oscillator construction; it asserts no existence statement outside that class, no explicit solution, no long-time or adiabatic statement, no measurement and no empirical comparison.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Chapter 5 printed pages 123-131 (PDF pages 135-143) and Section 9.1: strong evolution equations with a common domain of the generators

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 4.3-4.5 printed pages 30-39 (PDF pages 30-39): the forced harmonic oscillator, its translation operator and the classical response of coherent states

items.physical_scope: The common-domain driven model of the declared system: existence and uniqueness of a strong two-time propagator for a C^1 family of self-adjoint operators on a fixed dense domain Y, invariance of Y with a uniform graph bound, the strong Schroedinger equation on Y, the reverse and adjoint equations, and the admissibility of the declared driven oscillator family H(t) = H_osc - f(t) Q as an instance. The theorem is conditional on the common-domain regularity class; it asserts no laboratory realization, no measurement, no long-time or asymptotic statement and no empirical result.

items.title: The circularly driven two-level model: exact rotating-frame reduction, Rabi populations, resonance and inversion times
items.statement:
Adopt the framework data and the **declared circular two-level drive model** of clause (f) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]: $\mathfrak H=\mathbb C^{2}$ with the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ and the Pauli matrices $(\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z)$ of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), real parameters $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ and
$$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),\qquad t\in I=[t_{0},t_{1}],$$
read as the model's energy family in the bounded norm-continuous class, with $U_{\mathrm c}(t,s)$ its unique unitary propagator ([[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-bounded-norm-propagator]] clause (a)). Put $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$, $b:=\sqrt{\Delta^{2}+\Omega_{1}^{2}}$, let $R(t):=\cos(\omega t/2)I+i\sin(\omega t/2)\sigma_{z}$ be the rotating frame of [[lem-nrqm-driven-dynamics-two-level-rotating-frame]] and let $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ be the projections onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$, with populations $p_{\bullet}(t):=\langle P_{\bullet}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$ of the evolved vector. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Exact rotating-frame reduction.* For every solution $\psi$ of $i\hbar\psi'(t)=H_{\mathrm c}(t)\psi(t)$ the rotating-frame vector $\psi_{R}(t):=R(t)\psi(t)$ satisfies exactly
$$i\hbar\psi_{R}'(t)=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x}\bigr)\psi_{R}(t),$$
with the constant matrix $\frac{\hbar}{2}(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x})$; equivalently
$$U_{\mathrm c}(t,s)=R(t)^{*}\,e^{-i(t-s)(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x})/2}\,R(s)\qquad(s,t\in I).$$

(b) *Rabi populations.* Let $\psi(s)=e_{\uparrow}$ at time $s$. Define $p_{\bullet}^{R}(\tau):=\langle P_{\bullet}\psi_R(s+\tau),\psi_R(s+\tau)\rangle$ for $\tau\in I-s:=\{t-s:t\in I\}$. Then for $\tau:=t-s$
$$p_{\downarrow}(t)=p_{\downarrow}^{R}(\tau)=\Bigl|\bigl\langle e_{\downarrow},e^{-i\tau(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x})/2}e_{\uparrow}\bigr\rangle\Bigr|^{2}=\frac{\Omega_{1}^{2}}{b^{2}}\sin^{2}\!\Bigl(\frac{b\tau}{2}\Bigr)\qquad(b>0),$$
and $p_{\uparrow}(t)=1-p_{\downarrow}(t)$; the populations of the rotating-frame vector $\psi_{R}(t)$ are the same numbers.

(c) *Resonance and inversion times.* At resonance $\Delta=0$ one has $p_{\downarrow}(t)=\sin^{2}(\Omega_{1}\tau/2)$; when $\Omega_1\ne0$, the drive inverts the population fully at the **pi-pulse** time $\tau=\pi/|\Omega_{1}|$ and returns it to the initial level at $\tau=2\pi/|\Omega_{1}|$; for $b>0$ the population is exactly periodic in $\tau$ with period $2\pi/b$. For $\Omega_{1}=0$ the populations are constant, $p_{\downarrow}\equiv0$ and $p_{\uparrow}\equiv1$.

(d) *Scope.* The statements are exact for the declared finite model and its declared parameters; the rotating frame is a change of description of the same model and does not change the populations. The theorem asserts no damping or relaxation, no decoherence, no measurement record, no identification of $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1}$ with laboratory fields or of the two levels with a species, and no empirical value.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Sections 4-6 chapter pages 7-19 (PDF pages 7-19): the ammonia two-state oscillation, its probabilities, and the rotating-frame reduction of a circularly polarized magnetic drive to a time-independent Hamiltonian

items.physical_scope: The declared circular two-level drive model with splitting frequency omega0, transverse coupling Omega1 and drive frequency omega: the exact rotating-frame reduction to the constant matrix (hbar/2)(Delta sigma_z + Omega1 sigma_x), the exact level populations of the evolved up-state as Rabi probabilities, the resonance case and the pi-pulse and return times. The statement is exact for the declared finite model; it asserts no damping or relaxation, no measurement record, no laboratory identification of the parameters and no empirical result.

items.title: The linearly driven two-level model: rotating-wave approximation with an explicit finite-time error contract and the averaged Rabi populations
items.statement:
Adopt the framework data and the **declared linear two-level drive model** of clause (f) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]: $\mathfrak H=\mathbb C^{2}$, the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ and Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), real parameters $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ with $\omega\ne0$, and
$$H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}\bigr),\qquad t\in I=[a,b],$$
read as the model's energy family in the bounded norm-continuous class with unique propagator $U_{\mathrm l}(t,s)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-bounded-norm-propagator]] clause (a)). Put $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$, let $R(t):=\cos(\omega t/2)I+i\sin(\omega t/2)\sigma_{z}$ be the rotating frame of [[lem-nrqm-driven-dynamics-two-level-rotating-frame]], let $U_{\mathrm l}^{R}(t,s):=R(t)U_{\mathrm l}(t,s)R(s)^{*}$, and define the **averaged matrix** and the **counter-rotating amplitude**
$$A:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\frac{\Omega_{1}}{2}\sigma_{x}\Bigr),\qquad B:=\frac{\hbar\Omega_{1}}{8}\bigl(\sigma_{x}+i\sigma_{y}\bigr),\qquad \varepsilon(\tau):=\frac{|\Omega_{1}|}{2|\omega|}\Bigl[1+\tau\Bigl(\frac{|\Delta|}{2}+\frac{3|\Omega_{1}|}{4}\Bigr)\Bigr].$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Exact rotating-frame family.* For every $t\in I$,
$$R(t)H_{\mathrm l}(t)R(t)^{*}+i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}=A+e^{2i\omega t}B+e^{-2i\omega t}B^{*},$$
with $A=A^{*}$, $\|A/\hbar\|\le\frac12(|\Delta|+|\Omega_{1}|/2)$ and $\|B/\hbar\|=|\Omega_{1}|/4$; the second and third terms are the **counter-rotating terms** of the drive in the rotating frame.

(b) *Rotating-wave error contract.* For all $s,t\in I$, with $\tau:=|t-s|$,
$$\bigl\|U_{\mathrm l}^{R}(t,s)-e^{-i(t-s)A/\hbar}\bigr\|\le\varepsilon(\tau)=\frac{|\Omega_{1}|}{2|\omega|}\Bigl[1+\tau\Bigl(\frac{|\Delta|}{2}+\frac{3|\Omega_{1}|}{4}\Bigr)\Bigr];$$
the bound is uniform in $s$ for fixed $\tau$ and grows linearly in $\tau$.

(c) *Population comparison.* Let $\psi(s)=e_{\uparrow}$ and let $p_{\downarrow}(t):=\langle P_{\downarrow}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$ be the exact down-population at time $t$, where $\psi(t)=U_{\mathrm l}(t,s)e_{\uparrow}$. Let
$$p_{\downarrow}^{\mathrm{avg}}(\tau):=\frac{(\Omega_{1}/2)^{2}}{\Delta^{2}+(\Omega_{1}/2)^{2}}\,\sin^{2}\!\Bigl(\frac{\tau}{2}\sqrt{\Delta^{2}+\frac{\Omega_{1}^{2}}{4}}\Bigr)\qquad(\Omega_{1}\ne0),\qquad p_{\downarrow}^{\mathrm{avg}}\equiv0\quad(\Omega_{1}=0),$$
be the down-population of the initial up-state under the propagator of the **averaged family** $t\mapsto A$. Then for every $s,t\in I$
$$\bigl|p_{\downarrow}(t)-p_{\downarrow}^{\mathrm{avg}}(t-s)\bigr|\le 2\,\varepsilon(|t-s|).$$
At resonance $\Delta=0$ one has $p_{\downarrow}^{\mathrm{avg}}(\tau)=\sin^{2}(|\Omega_{1}|\tau/4)$.

(d) *Scope.* The averaged family is not asserted to be the model's exact dynamics: clause (b) is an error contract bounding the exact rotating-frame propagator against it, and its linear growth in $\tau$ gives no uniform-in-time approximation. The theorem asserts no resonance width, no decay rate, no long-time limit, no measurement record, no laboratory identification and no empirical result.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Section 5 chapter pages 14-15 (PDF pages 14-15): the linearly oscillating ammonia drive, the decomposition E(t) = E0 (exp(i omega0 t) + exp(-i omega0 t)) and the dropping of the counter-rotating terms

items.physical_scope: The declared linear two-level drive model: the exact rotating-frame family with its co- and counter-rotating parts, the rotating-wave error contract bounding the rotating-frame propagator against the propagator of the averaged detuned Rabi matrix, and the resulting bound on the exact level population against the averaged Rabi probability. The statement is conditional on the declared finite model and on a nonzero drive frequency; the error bound is linear in the elapsed time and the theorem asserts no uniform-in-time approximation, no decay, no measurement and no empirical result.

items.title: The declared adiabatic protocol model: slow parameter, followed spectral subspace, uniform gap and leakage probability
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the framework data and readings of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clauses (a), (d) (P1, P2 and P4 and their state, observable and evolution readings; units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]); assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral and evolution suppliers. The autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 is adopted in the reading of [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]; the protocol below is the reading of its clause (iv) for slowly varying families.

**(b) The declared slow family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair, fix a **protocol duration** $T>0$ (seconds), the **slow parameter** $s\in[0,1]$, and a family $s\mapsto H(s)$ of self-adjoint operators on the declared state space $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), read as the model's **energy at slow time $s$**, in one of the two declared regularity branches:
- **(f) finite branch.** $\mathfrak H=\mathbb C^{d}$ for some $d\ge1$ and $H\in C^{2}([0,1];\operatorname{Herm}(\mathbb C^{d}))$;
- **(u) common-domain branch.** $D(H(s))=Y$ for a dense subspace $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ that is a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$, every $H(s)$ is self-adjoint on $\mathfrak H$, and $s\mapsto H(s)$ is of class $C^{1}([0,1];\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]).

The family is prescribed model data: no laboratory ramp, field source or feedback is assumed. The **protocol propagator** is the unique unitary family $U_{T}(s,\sigma)$ on $\mathfrak H$ solving the slow-time Schroedinger equation
$$i\hbar\,\partial_{s}U_{T}(s,\sigma)=T\,H(s)U_{T}(s,\sigma),\qquad U_{T}(\sigma,\sigma)=I,\qquad 0\le\sigma\le s\le1,$$
whose existence is cited from the mathematics: in branch (f) the family $s\mapsto TH(s)/\hbar$ is norm-continuous with bounded self-adjoint values and $U_T$ is its Dyson propagator ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]]), and in branch (u) the family $s\mapsto TH(s)/\hbar$ lies in $C^{1}([0,1];\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$ and $U_T$ is its strong propagator ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]]). The model's evolution in physical time is $\psi(t):=U_{T}(t/T,0)\psi(0)$ for $t\in[0,T]$, and the evolved preparation is $\rho(t):=U_{T}(t/T,0)\rho(0)U_{T}(t/T,0)^{*}$, read as in clause (d) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]].

**(c) Followed spectral subspace and uniform gap.** Fix a **label**: for branch (f) a spectral cluster $\sigma_{P}(s)\subseteq\sigma(H(s))$ ([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]]) with spectral projection $P(s)$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and for branch (u) a fixed finite-multiplicity eigenvalue $E(s)$ of $H(s)$ with spectral projection $P(s)$. The label is declared **uniformly gapped** when
$$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(\sigma_{P}(s),\,\sigma(H(s))\setminus\sigma_{P}(s)\bigr)\ge g>0\qquad(s\in[0,1])$$
in branch (f), respectively $\operatorname{dist}(E(s),\sigma(H(s))\setminus\{E(s)\})\ge g>0$ in branch (u), and **coherently followed** when $s\mapsto P(s)$ is continuous in operator norm and coincides with the local Riesz continuation of $P(0)$ (in branch (f): the spectral projection of $H(s)$ for the cluster continuously connected to the initial one). A **preparation in the subspace** is a preparation with $\rho(0)$ supported in $\operatorname{ran}P(0)$; for a unit vector $\psi(0)\in\operatorname{ran}P(0)$ the **leakage probability** at slow time $s$ is the model's outcome probability
$$p_{\mathrm{leak}}(s):=\mu^{(I-P(s))}_{\psi(sT)}(\{1\})=\bigl\|(I-P(s))\psi(sT)\bigr\|^{2},\qquad \psi(sT)=U_{T}(s,0)\psi(0),$$
that is, the Born probability in the reading of P2 that the evolved preparation is found outside the followed subspace at slow time $s$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]; [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).

**(d) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(c) adopt the protocol as an idealization and fix its vocabulary. The size of the leakage is not part of the definition: it is the content of the adiabatic theorems of the page, which are conditional on the uniform gap and on coherent following. The definition asserts no claim that a laboratory ramp realizes the family, no selection or relaxation of a branch by the protocol, no thermalization, no measurement record and no empirical result; whether a laboratory preparation realizes a preparation in the declared subspace is a tested identification in the sense of P7.

items.title: Finite-dimensional gapped protocol: the 1/T leakage estimate, the intertwining propagator and the Born leakage probability
items.statement:
Adopt the declared adiabatic protocol of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-adiabatic-protocol]] in its **finite branch (f)**: $\mathfrak H=\mathbb C^{d}$ for some $d\ge1$, $H\in C^{2}([0,1];\operatorname{Herm}(\mathbb C^{d}))$, $T>0$ and $U_{T}(s,\sigma)$ the protocol propagator, and let $P(s)$ be the spectral projection of $H(s)$ for a spectral cluster $\sigma_{P}(s)$ that is **uniformly gapped** with
$$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(\sigma_{P}(s),\sigma(H(s))\setminus\sigma_{P}(s)\bigr)\ge g>0\qquad(s\in[0,1])$$
and **coherently followed** in the sense of the protocol definition (continuity in operator norm, equivalently the local Riesz continuation of $P(0)$). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Regularity of the followed cluster.* $P\in C^{2}([0,1];\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^{d}))$, the commutator $K(s):=[P'(s),P(s)]$ is anti-Hermitian of class $C^{1}$ with $[K(s),P(s)]=P'(s)$, and there is a $C^{1}$ Hermitian family $X(s)$ with $[H(s),X(s)]=K(s)$ for every $s\in[0,1]$.

(b) *Intertwining.* Let $U_{A}$ solve $i\,\partial_{s}U_{A}(s)=(TH(s)/\hbar+iK(s))U_{A}(s)$, $U_{A}(0)=I$ (equivalently $U_{A}'=(-iTH/\hbar+K)U_{A}$). Then $P(s)U_{A}(s)=U_{A}(s)P(0)$ for every $s\in[0,1]$.

(c) *Leakage estimate.* With
$$C:=\hbar\Bigl(2\sup_{s\in[0,1]}\|X(s)\|+\int_{0}^{1}\bigl(\|X'(s)\|+\|K(s)\|\,\|X(s)\|\bigr)\,ds\Bigr)<\infty,$$
one has, for every $s\in[0,1]$,
$$\bigl\|(I-P(s))U_{T}(s)P(0)\bigr\|\le\frac{C}{T},$$
and therefore, for every unit vector $\psi(0)\in\operatorname{ran}P(0)$ with $\psi(sT)=U_{T}(s,0)\psi(0)$,
$$p_{\mathrm{leak}}(s)=\bigl\|(I-P(s))\psi(sT)\bigr\|^{2}\le\frac{C^{2}}{T^{2}},\qquad \bigl\langle P(s)\psi(sT),\psi(sT)\bigr\rangle\ge1-\frac{C^{2}}{T^{2}} .$$ The same Born leakage and survival bounds hold for every supported mixed preparation $\rho_0=P(0)\rho_0P(0)$, with $\rho(s)=U_T(s,0)\rho_0U_T(s,0)^*$ and $p_{\rm leak}(s)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(s)(I-P(s)))$.

(d) *Scope.* The estimate is conditional on the uniform positive gap, on coherent following and on the finite branch; the constant $C$ depends on the family and its label, not on $T$. The theorem asserts no statement for gap-closing families, no unbounded or common-domain family (which is the subject of the companion theorem), no laboratory protocol, no branch selection or relaxation, and no empirical result.

items.title: The slowly varying one-centre Coulomb source: verified uniform gap of the n-th level and the 1/T leakage estimate
items.statement:
Adopt the declared one-centre Coulomb model of [[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with mass parameter $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and declared coupling $\kappa>0$ of unit $\mathrm{J\,m}$, and its energy operator $H_{\kappa}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}C_{\gamma}$, $C_{\gamma}=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $Y=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with $\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$. Adopt the declared adiabatic protocol of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-adiabatic-protocol]] in its common-domain branch (u) with the following **declared source-strength family**: a prescribed path $\kappa\in C^{2}([0,1];(0,\infty))$ with $0<\kappa_{\min}\le\kappa(s)\le\kappa_{\max}<\infty$, the family
$$H(s):=H_{\kappa(s)},\qquad \gamma(s):=\frac{2m\kappa(s)}{\hbar^{2}},\qquad A(s):=-\Delta-\frac{\gamma(s)}{|\cdot|},\qquad D(A(s))=Y,$$
read as the model's energy at slow time $s$, a protocol duration $T>0$ (seconds), and the protocol propagator $U_{T}$ defined by $i\hbar\partial_{s}U_{T}(s,\sigma)=TH(s)U_{T}(s,\sigma)$, $U_{T}(\sigma,\sigma)=I$. For this prescribed positive $C^{2}$ path, the exact common domain, uniform graph-norm equivalence and $C^{2}([0,1];\mathcal B(Y,L^{2}))$ regularity are consequences of the Coulomb bound, proved below; they require no additional admissibility assumption on the path. Fix $n\ge1$ and let $P_{n}(s)$ be the spectral projection of $H(s)$ for its $n$-th level. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Level, degeneracy and uniform gap.* For every $s\in[0,1]$ the number
$$E_{n}(s)=-\frac{m\kappa(s)^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Bigl(-\frac{\gamma(s)^{2}}{4n^{2}}\Bigr)$$
is an eigenvalue of $H(s)$ with eigenspace of dimension $n^{2}$, the spectrum of $H(s)$ has no eigenvalues in $[0,\infty)$, its essential spectrum is $[0,\infty)$, and the complementary distance of the level is bounded below uniformly by
$$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(E_{n}(s),\sigma(H(s))\setminus\{E_{n}(s)\}\bigr)\ \ge\ \frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,\delta_{n}\,\gamma_{\min}^{2}\ =:\ g_{n}\ >\ 0,\qquad \delta_{n}:=\frac{2n+1}{4n^{2}(n+1)^{2}},\qquad \gamma_{\min}=\frac{2m\kappa_{\min}}{\hbar^{2}} .$$
Consequently $P_n\in C^2([0,1];\mathcal B(L^2,Y))$, and the family of projections $s\mapsto P_{n}(s)$ is a uniformly gapped, coherently followed label of the protocol in the sense of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-adiabatic-protocol]] clause (c).

(b) *Leakage estimate.* There is a constant $C_{n}<\infty$, depending only on $n$, on the mass parameter $m$, on $\hbar$ and on $\kappa_{\min},\kappa_{\max}$ and the $C^{2}$ norm of the path $\kappa$ (that is, on the data of the declared family), such that for every $s\in[0,1]$
$$\bigl\|(I-P_{n}(s))U_{T}(s,0)P_{n}(0)\bigr\|\le\frac{C_{n}}{T},$$
and therefore, for every unit vector $\psi(0)\in\operatorname{ran}P_{n}(0)$ with $\psi(t)=U_{T}(t/T,0)\psi(0)$,
$$p_{\mathrm{leak}}(s)=\bigl\|(I-P_{n}(s))\psi(sT)\bigr\|^{2}\le\frac{C_{n}^{2}}{T^{2}},\qquad \bigl\langle P_{n}(s)\psi(sT),\psi(sT)\bigr\rangle\ge1-\frac{C_{n}^{2}}{T^{2}} .$$ The same Born leakage and survival bounds hold for every supported mixed preparation $\rho_0=P_n(0)\rho_0P_n(0)$, with $\rho(s)=U_T(s,0)\rho_0U_T(s,0)^*$ and $p_{\rm leak}(s)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(s)(I-P_n(s)))$.

(c) *Scope.* The theorem concerns the declared external-source family only: the coupling path is a prescribed source strength of the one-centre model, not an applied laboratory field, and the statement asserts no laboratory control, no linear Stark coupling (which has no uniformly gapped branch), no transition rate, no branch selection or relaxation, and no empirical result.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the page: what is adopted, what is proved, and what is excluded
items.statement:
## What the page adopts

The page works inside the framework's postulates P1, P2, P4 and P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and adopts, as additional model assumptions, the driven-dynamics reading of clause (iv) of P4 in [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]: a prescribed time-dependent self-adjoint energy family in one of three regularity classes, carried by a unitary two-time propagator, with the evolved preparation and outcome-law readings and with the two declared two-level drive models of its clause (f). [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-interaction-picture]] fixes the interaction-picture readings, and [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-adiabatic-protocol]] fixes the slow-family protocol, its followed spectral subspace and its leakage probability. All three are readings and model assumptions, not derived statements.

## What the page proves

[[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-bounded-norm-propagator]] proves well-posedness, the Dyson truncation budget and the outcome-law error in the bounded norm-continuous class; [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-mild-propagator-and-pictures]] proves the mild propagator and the equivalence of the Schroedinger and interaction readings in the bounded-control class; [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-first-order-transition-amplitude]] proves the first-order amplitude with its explicit Dyson remainder and the closed sinusoidal drive with the co- and counter-rotating parts and the linear-in-time resonant growth; [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-common-domain-propagator]] proves the strong propagator and its domain invariance in the common-domain class and verifies the driven oscillator as an instance; [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-circular-drive-exact-rabi]] proves the exact rotating-frame reduction and Rabi populations of the declared circular two-level model; [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-linear-drive-rotating-wave-error]] proves the rotating-wave error contract for the linearly polarized model with the bound on the population difference; and [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-finite-adiabatic-leakage]] and [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-coulomb-adiabatic-leakage]] prove the $1/T$ leakage estimates in the finite and Coulomb-family branches. Every one of these is a conditional consequence of the adopted model data, the cited mathematics and P1, P2 and P4.

## What the page excludes

The page asserts no open-system or environment coupling, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no thermalization or equilibration, no Fermi golden rule, no transition rate, no exponential decay, no resonance width, no spontaneous emission, no measurement or apparatus model and no branch selection by a ramping protocol; in particular the rotating-wave contract of [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-linear-drive-rotating-wave-error]] is linear in the elapsed time and gives no uniform-in-time approximation, the first-order amplitude theorem is a finite-time statement with an explicit remainder, and the adiabatic theorems are conditional on a uniform positive gap and coherent following. The uncompressed linear Stark coupling is not a bounded perturbation and does not appear.

## Empirical status

The page records no experiment, no measured population, rate, frequency or lifetime, and no uncertainty record; its sources are mathematical and textbook treatments of the models, not experimental reports, so no measured value, no sampling model and no statistical inference enters any statement. The identification of a laboratory two-level system, spin, molecule or slowly varying source with the declared models and their parameters is a tested identification in the sense of P7 with its own uncertainty; agreement of a model computation with data would be evidence about the combined model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework.

items.title: The two-level inversion model in an oscillating field: resonance, averaged Rabi inversion and its error contract
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2 and P4 in the readings of the declared driven model ([[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clause (a)) and the basis $(|{\mathrm E}\rangle,|{\mathrm G}\rangle)$ of a **declared two-level inversion model**: two orthogonal unit vectors with the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) acting on their span, so that $\sigma_{z}=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ distinguishes the two levels. Declare real parameters $\Delta_{0}>0$ (half the inversion splitting, joules), $\mu>0$ (a dipole-like coupling, in $\mathrm{C\,m}$), $E_{0}>0$ (a field amplitude, in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$) and a drive frequency $\omega>0$ in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, and declare the model's energy family
$$H(t):=\Delta_{0}\sigma_{z}+2\mu E_{0}\cos(\omega t)\,\sigma_{x},\qquad t\in\mathbb R,$$
read as the energy of the declared model, with $\hbar$ the reduced Planck constant of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; populations are the diagonal entries of the two projections onto $\mathbb C|{\mathrm E}\rangle$ and $\mathbb C|{\mathrm G}\rangle$ in the evolved preparation. Fix the **coupling ratio** $x:=\mu E_{0}/\Delta_{0}$ (dimensionless). Then:

(a) *Identification with the declared linear drive.* $H(t)=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x})$ with
$$\omega_{0}=\frac{2\Delta_{0}}{\hbar},\qquad \Omega_{1}=\frac{4\mu E_{0}}{\hbar},\qquad \omega_{0}\in\mathrm{s^{-1}},\ \Omega_{1}\in\mathrm{s^{-1}},$$
so the model is an instance of the declared linear two-level drive model of clause (f) with $\Delta=\omega_{0}-\omega$; the level splitting is $2\Delta_{0}$.

(b) *Resonance and averaged inversion.* At resonance $\omega=\omega_{0}$, i.e. $\hbar\omega=2\Delta_{0}$, the averaged model of the page's error contract predicts that the initial $|{\mathrm E}\rangle$ population is transferred to $|{\mathrm G}\rangle$ with probability
$$p_{\mathrm G}^{\mathrm{avg}}(\tau)=\sin^{2}\!\Bigl(\frac{\mu E_{0}\tau}{\hbar}\Bigr),$$
which equals $1$ at the **inversion time** $\tau=\pi\hbar/(2\mu E_{0})$; equivalently $\Omega_{1}\tau/4=\pi/2$ at that time.

(c) *Error contract at inversion.* At the inversion time $\tau=\pi\hbar/(2\mu E_{0})$ the exact $|{\mathrm G}\rangle$ population $p_{\mathrm G}$ satisfies
$$\bigl|p_{\mathrm G}-1\bigr|\le 2x\Bigl(1+\frac{3\pi}{2}\Bigr),$$
so with the declared ratio $x=1/100$ the contract gives $p_{\mathrm G}\ge1-\frac{2+3\pi}{100}$;

(d) *status.* The model, its parameters and the time $\tau$ are declared model data; no measured transition frequency, no laboratory molecule, cavity or field, no damping or relaxation and no measurement record appears, and the averaged formula is accompanied by the explicit contract of clause (c), not asserted as exact.

items.title: The driven oscillator: exact classical response of a coherent preparation and stationary fluctuations
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2 and P4 in the readings of the declared driven model ([[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clause (a)) and the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (b), (c) with parameters $m,\omega,\hbar>0$, length scale $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{osc}},\mathrm J)$ and position and momentum observables $(Q,\mathrm m)$, $(P,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$; adopt the coherent-state family $(\Psi_{z})_{z\in\mathbb C}$ of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]] and the **driven oscillator family**
$$H(t):=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q,\qquad t\in[a,b],$$
with a declared drive $f\in C^{1}([a,b];\mathbb R)$ read in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$, as an instance of the protocol's common-domain model of [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-common-domain-propagator]] clause (c). Let $U(t,s)$ be the unique strong propagator of that family (which preserves $Y=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$), and let $(q(\cdot;s),p(\cdot;s))$ be the classical forced response with zero data at $s$:
$$q'=\frac{p}{m},\qquad p'=-m\omega^{2}q+f,\qquad q(s)=p(s)=0 .$$
Then for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and $s,t\in[a,b]$, with $\langle A\rangle(t):=\langle AU(t,s)\Psi_{z},U(t,s)\Psi_{z}\rangle$:

(a) *Exact classical mean position and momentum.*
$$\langle Q\rangle(t)=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}\bigl(ze^{-i\omega(t-s)}\bigr)+q(t;s),\qquad \langle P\rangle(t)=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(ze^{-i\omega(t-s)}\bigr)+p(t;s);$$

(b) *Stationary fluctuations.* the preparation spreads of position and momentum in the evolved coherent preparation are
$$\Delta Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta Q\,\Delta P=\frac{\hbar}{2},$$
independent of $t$ and of $f$;

(c) *Undriven check.* if $f\equiv0$ then $q\equiv p\equiv0$ and the means reduce to the free classical rotation $\bigl(\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}(ze^{-i\omega(t-s)}),\ \frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}(ze^{-i\omega(t-s)})\bigr)$ of the coherent label;

(d) *status.* The statements are exact for the declared model and drive; no laboratory oscillator, drive source, damping or measurement record is asserted.

items.title: What the examples check, what they do not contain, and the empirical status of the companion page
items.statement:
## What the examples check

[[ex-nrqm-driven-dynamics-circular-drive-exact-populations]] checks the exact Rabi populations of the declared circular two-level model at rational multiples of the Rabi period, including the quarter-inversion value $1/2$, the pi-pulse value $1$, the return value $0$ and a detuned value $1/4$; [[ex-nrqm-driven-dynamics-linear-drive-rotating-wave-budget]] evaluates the rotating-wave error contract of [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-linear-drive-rotating-wave-error]] at declared dimensionless times, including one exact rational averaged population and the observation that the contract is conservative at the initial time; [[ex-nrqm-driven-dynamics-ammonia-two-level-resonance]] matches the declared linear model onto an inversion-doublet family with an oscillating field, computes the averaged inversion probability and its pulse time and evaluates the error contract there for a declared coupling ratio; and [[ex-nrqm-driven-dynamics-driven-oscillator-coherent-response]] checks the exact classical mean response and the stationary fluctuations of a coherent preparation of the driven oscillator of [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-common-domain-propagator]] clause (c).

## What the examples do not contain

The examples contain no measured frequency, energy, population, rate or lifetime; no apparatus, detector, calibration, sampling model or uncertainty record; no damping, relaxation, decoherence or environmental coupling; no identification of a laboratory spin, molecule, cavity or oscillator with the declared models or of a laboratory field with the declared drive parameters; and no claim that any declared parameter value is realized in nature. They also contain no Fermi golden rule, no continuum density of states and no long-time limit, in agreement with the scope of the companion A page ([[rem-nrqm-driven-dynamics-scope-and-empirical-status]]).

## Empirical status

All four examples are conditional computations inside declared models: their inputs are declared parameters, the cited mathematics and the postulates P1, P2 and P4. The sources cited are mathematical and textbook treatments, not experimental reports, so no empirical premise and no statistical inference enters any statement of the page. Comparing any of these model outputs with a laboratory oscillation or pulse would require a separately declared preparation and apparatus model with its own uncertainty and would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions; it is a tested identification in the sense of P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of the computations here.
